newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bodies those of missing German couple, police say.
newsitem.headline: Bodies those of missing German couple, police say.

text.p: German police said on Thursday they were almost certain two bodies found in the boot of a wealthy sausage manufacturer's car were those of the businessman and his wife, who had been missing since Monday.

A police spokesman said the bodies found in the grey Mercedes in a suburb of Dortmund, western Germany, were "with all probability verging on certainty" those of Peter Schulte-Berthold, 43, and his wife Christine, 37.
Police said they had detained one person in connection with the deaths. The bodies, which lay in a pool of blood, both bore stab wounds and a knife had been found in the car.
Police had discovered traces of human blood in the couple's house in Witten, and a large pool of blood in the garage. Two plane tickets to Budapest were found lying on the kitchen table.
The police spokesman said Schulte-Berthold had been killed outdoors while his wife had died inside the house.
Schulte-Berthold was managing director of Zimmerman sausage factory, part of an extensive holding company of 18 firms.
Police declined to give any details on the person they had detained or on a possible motive for the killings.
